source_snapshot.procedure: Change different Time zone; generic setup says clear logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Copied text says date/time changes after setting Daylight saving time.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL follows the Time Zone title through WebUI and time readback but silently ignores the copied DST criterion, does not define zones/UTC invariance or distinguish regional timezone metadata from the standard SEL UTC offset.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires explicit source/target zones, UTC normalization, DST/NTP behavior, event boundaries and restoration, but the historical V3.1 record retained the copied criterion as an open conflict.

old_problem: Items/Procedure and the referenced UTC-offset Script identify timezone work, while Criteria copies the preceding DST case. Timezone selection, a fixed SEL UTC offset and DST rules are related but non-equivalent; silently treating any visible shift as all three would both lose the row's identity and duplicate the separate DST case.
disposition_reason: Reconcile the copied criterion using convergent case-specific evidence: the item and procedure say Time Zone, the Script explicitly names SEL time UTC offset, and row 919 independently owns DST. The Review-layer acceptance therefore verifies an approved source→target timezone/local-offset change while preserving UTC and event ordering; it records DST interaction but does not claim DST coverage. The standard SEL UTC-offset readback is a separate corroborating surface, not proof of a regional IANA zone. Master text and Script history remain unchanged and visible.
decision_basis: XLSX row 920, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, selection manifest, separate preceding DST case, Script URL and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed.

Three independent fields—Items, Procedure and Script name—converge on timezone/UTC-offset intent, while the criterion exactly repeats the distinct preceding DST topic; Review-layer correction resolves rather than conceals the source defect.
IPMI v2.0 defines SEL Time UTC Offset as signed minutes from UTC to SEL Time and distinguishes it from absolute SEL Time; a fixed offset does not by itself prove a regional zone or DST rule.

Local representation should change according to the selected zone/offset while the underlying UTC instant and event ordering remain within tolerance unless authoritative vendor semantics explicitly say otherwise.

test_case.test_name: Verify BMC timezone selection with UTC invariance and separate SEL UTC-offset evidence
test_case.purpose: Verify an approved BMC source-to-target timezone change through the supported control changes the visible local time and timezone metadata by the documented offset while preserving the correct UTC instant, NTP policy and event chronology; independently record the standard SEL UTC-offset behavior and avoid claiming the separate DST test.
required_package: Exact BMC asset/firmware/WebUI identity and vendor documentation for supported named zones or fixed-offset model and affected clock/log surfaces
Approved source and target IANA zone identifiers or fixed offsets, exact expected offset difference, current DST state and numeric tolerance
Trusted UTC reference plus current WebUI/API/SEL/local/UTC values, timezone metadata and NTP/synchronization policy
Pinned reviewed revision of the source Script with target, raw-command number, signed-minute encoding, byte order, get/set symmetry and rollback verified before any use
Authorized WebUI operator, visual evidence and preserved audit/SEL event-boundary collection
Time-sensitive impact approval and exact original timezone/offset/DST/NTP restoration plan
test_case.test_command: STATE-CHANGING; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT APPROVAL. Preserve logs and record the verified target's WebUI timezone identifier/offset, DST/NTP state, trusted UTC reference, supported API/SEL offset and event boundary. Pin and inspect the referenced Script; never guess raw fields. Choose one approved target zone or offset and calculate the expected local-time difference. Obtain approval, save it once through the source control path, and capture visual WebUI plus audit evidence. Re-read metadata and normalized clocks immediately and after settling: verify the local representation changes by the expected offset while UTC remains within tolerance. If the reviewed Script/standard SEL UTC-offset path is in scope, record its signed-minute value separately and do not equate it with a regional zone. Restore the exact original policy; do not clear logs, modify DST as a substitute or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: The target timezone/offset is visibly saved and read back, local display changes by the calculated source→target difference, the normalized UTC instant and event ordering remain within approved tolerance, and NTP/DST interaction matches documented policy. The SEL UTC offset, when supported/in scope, equals the expected signed-minute value for that surface. Original policy is restored, and the outcome explicitly states that timezone PASS does not pass the separate DST case.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact source/target metadata, calculated versus observed local offset, stable UTC reference within tolerance, visual/audit proof, documented NTP/DST interaction, event chronology and restoration. A displayed time shift, copied DST criterion or raw offset alone cannot pass. Wrong zone/encoding/offset, unexpected UTC mutation, event disorder, NTP overwrite or failed restoration is FAIL. Missing zones, tolerance, Script review, approval or recovery is NOT READY. DST transition/rule coverage is explicitly excluded from this verdict.
safety_gate: Do not clear SEL/audit logs; preserve local and UTC boundary evidence before and after the change.
Do not choose arbitrary zones, equate IANA zones with fixed offsets, or use a DST toggle to satisfy timezone coverage.
Review and pin the internal Script before use; validate signed-minute units, byte order, exact target and rollback rather than guessing OEM/raw parameters.
Do not change absolute time, host timezone or NTP/DST policy outside the approved scope; obtain point-of-action approval before the one save/write.
Stop on unexpected UTC mutation, wrong offset, synchronization overwrite or chronology mismatch; do not automatically write again.
expected_evidence: Source-conflict reconciliation, target/version identity, approved source/target zone or offset, expected difference, tolerance and DST/NTP policy
Pinned reviewed Script revision and standard/vendor semantics showing exact target, signed-minute encoding, byte order and rollback
Visual WebUI before/entered/save/after timezone evidence and BMC audit event
Trusted reference and normalized WebUI/API/SEL/local/UTC values before, immediately after and settled with expected-versus-observed calculation
First post-change event ordering, separate SEL UTC-offset evidence and explicit timezone-versus-DST coverage statement
Original-policy restoration, preserved logs, no-retry proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong zone/offset, unexpected UTC shift, NTP overwrite or audit-order problem, stop and preserve UI/raw/audit/SEL evidence. Restore the exact original timezone/offset/DST/NTP policy through the verified path only after fresh authorization, then re-read normalized local and UTC values. Do not clear logs or repeat trial writes.

source_conflict.reason: The Review layer corrects the isolated copied DST criterion to timezone-specific acceptance because Items, Procedure and referenced UTC-offset Script agree and the adjacent source row separately preserves DST coverage. The original contradictory text remains immutable and traceable; no DST result is claimed here.
